paragraphs.title: Isaac Blesses Jacob and Sends Him Away

easy.question: Whom did Isaac command Jacob not to marry?
answers: The daughters of Canaan
The daughters of Egypt
The daughters of Moab
easy.explanation: Isaac commanded Jacob, “Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.”

easy.question: Where did Isaac command Jacob to go?
answers: To the land of Canaan
To Padanaram
To Egypt
easy.explanation: Isaac told Jacob, “Arise, go to Padanaram.”

easy.question: Who sent Jacob to Padanaram?
answers: Laban
Bethuel
Isaac
easy.explanation: At the end of the passage, it says, “And Isaac sent away Jacob.”

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in this passage?
answers: Isaac blesses and commands Jacob, and then Jacob leaves for Padanaram
Jacob leaves for Padanaram, and then Isaac commands him
Laban sends Jacob, and then Isaac blesses him
medium.explanation: First Isaac calls Jacob, blesses him, and gives him instructions; afterward he sends him away, and Jacob leaves.

medium.question: What does the phrase “the land wherein thou art a stranger” mean in context?
answers: The land where you will fight
The land where you live or stay
The land from which you will flee
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the land where Jacob is living or staying as a foreigner.

medium.question: What two main things are included in the blessing Isaac requests for Jacob?
answers: Wealth and victory in war
Wisdom and long life
Many descendants and the inheritance of the land
medium.explanation: Isaac asks that Jacob become fruitful and multiply, and that he inherit the land given to Abraham.

challenge.question: What was Laban’s family relationship to Rebekah?
answers: Laban was Rebekah’s brother
Laban was Rebekah’s father
Laban was Rebekah’s son
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies Laban as Rebekah’s brother.

challenge.question: How are Isaac’s marriage command and blessing connected?
answers: Jacob had to leave his family in order to give up the blessing
Jacob was sent to establish a suitable family and continue Abraham’s blessing
Jacob was sent only to find a new place to live
challenge.explanation: Isaac connects finding a wife from Rebekah’s family with continuing Abraham’s blessing of descendants and land.

challenge.question: Which precise detail about Jacob’s destination appears in verse 5?
answers: Jacob was sent to Isaac’s house in Canaan
Jacob was sent to Esau in Egypt
Jacob went to Padanaram, to Laban the son of Bethuel
challenge.explanation: The verse says Jacob went to Padanaram, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Syrian, Rebekah’s brother.

questions.question: What was Laban’s family relationship to Rebekah?
answers: Laban was Rebekah’s brother
Laban was Rebekah’s father
Laban was Rebekah’s son
questions.explanation: The verse identifies Laban as Rebekah’s brother.

questions.question: How are Isaac’s marriage command and blessing connected?
answers: Jacob had to leave his family in order to give up the blessing
Jacob was sent to establish a suitable family and continue Abraham’s blessing
Jacob was sent only to find a new place to live
questions.explanation: Isaac connects finding a wife from Rebekah’s family with continuing Abraham’s blessing of descendants and land.

questions.question: Which precise detail about Jacob’s destination appears in verse 5?
answers: Jacob was sent to Isaac’s house in Canaan
Jacob was sent to Esau in Egypt
Jacob went to Padanaram, to Laban the son of Bethuel
questions.explanation: The verse says Jacob went to Padanaram, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Syrian, Rebekah’s brother.

easy.question: Who sent Jacob to Padanaram?
answers: Isaac
Esau
Ishmael
easy.explanation: Isaac sent Jacob to Padanaram to take a wife from there.

easy.question: What did Isaac command Jacob concerning a wife?
answers: To take a wife from the daughters of Canaan
Not to take a wife from the daughters of Canaan
Not to take a wife at all
easy.explanation: Isaac commanded Jacob not to take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

easy.question: Whom did Esau take as a wife?
answers: Rebekah
Isaac’s daughter
Mahalath, Ishmael’s daughter
easy.explanation: Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath, Ishmael’s daughter, as his wife.

medium.question: Why did Jacob go to Padanaram?
answers: To fight Ishmael
To obey his parents and find a wife
To visit Esau
medium.explanation: Jacob obeyed his father and mother and went to Padanaram to take a wife from there.

medium.question: What does the phrase “the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac” mean in context?
answers: They were wealthy
They were far away
Isaac did not approve of them
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that Isaac was displeased with Esau’s Canaanite wives.

medium.question: What happened after Jacob obeyed his father and mother and went to Padanaram?
answers: Esau realized that the daughters of Canaan did not please Isaac
Isaac went to Ishmael
Jacob immediately returned home
medium.explanation: After describing Jacob’s departure, the passage says that Esau understood Isaac did not approve of the daughters of Canaan.

challenge.question: Why does it appear that Esau took Mahalath, Ishmael’s daughter, as a wife?
answers: Because Isaac told him to go to Ishmael
Because he wanted to correct the problem Isaac saw with his Canaanite wives
Because Jacob asked him to marry
challenge.explanation: Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan did not please Isaac, so he took a wife from Ishmael’s family instead.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “he took unto the wives which he had” show about Esau’s marriage?
answers: He divorced his earlier wives
He took Mahalath instead of all his other wives
He added Mahalath to his earlier wives
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that Mahalath was added to the wives Esau already had.

challenge.question: What family detail does the verse give about Mahalath?
answers: She was Ishmael’s daughter, Abraham’s son, and Nebajoth’s sister
She was Isaac’s daughter and Jacob’s sister
She was Canaan’s daughter and Rebekah’s sister
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies Mahalath as the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, and the sister of Nebajoth.

questions.question: Why does it appear that Esau took Mahalath, Ishmael’s daughter, as a wife?
answers: Because Isaac told him to go to Ishmael
Because he wanted to correct the problem Isaac saw with his Canaanite wives
Because Jacob asked him to marry
questions.explanation: Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan did not please Isaac, so he took a wife from Ishmael’s family instead.

questions.question: What does the phrase “he took unto the wives which he had” show about Esau’s marriage?
answers: He divorced his earlier wives
He took Mahalath instead of all his other wives
He added Mahalath to his earlier wives
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that Mahalath was added to the wives Esau already had.

questions.question: What family detail does the verse give about Mahalath?
answers: She was Ishmael’s daughter, Abraham’s son, and Nebajoth’s sister
She was Isaac’s daughter and Jacob’s sister
She was Canaan’s daughter and Rebekah’s sister
questions.explanation: The verse identifies Mahalath as the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, and the sister of Nebajoth.

easy.question: Who went out from Beersheba?
answers: Jacob
Isaac
Abraham
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Jacob went out from Beersheba.”

easy.question: Where did Jacob go?
answers: Jerusalem
Haran
Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that Jacob went toward Haran.

easy.question: What did Jacob do after the sun had set?
answers: He returned to Beersheba
He built a house
He lay down to sleep in that place
easy.explanation: After the sun had set, Jacob took stones for his pillows and lay down in that place.

medium.question: Why did Jacob stay there for the night?
answers: Because the sun had set
Because it began to rain
Because he met his family
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says that he stayed there all night because the sun was set.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Jacob lay down, took stones, and then set out
Jacob left Beersheba, went toward Haran, and stayed there for the night
Jacob reached Haran, returned to Beersheba, and then slept
medium.explanation: Jacob first left Beersheba, traveled toward Haran, and then stayed at a place overnight.

medium.question: In the phrase “and tarried there all night,” what does “tarried” mean?
answers: He fought there
He left immediately
He remained there for the night
medium.explanation: In this verse, “tarried” means that Jacob stayed there overnight.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “he lighted upon a certain place” mean in context?
answers: Jacob came upon a place during his journey
Jacob struck a person
Jacob built the place
challenge.explanation: Here the phrase means that Jacob arrived at or came upon a place during his journey.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Jacob putting stones under his head?
answers: He slept in a well-furnished house
He was sleeping outdoors and used stones as a support for his head
He gathered stones to build a city
challenge.explanation: The passage describes no bed or house, so Jacob apparently used stones as a support beneath his head.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Jacob stopped because of the time of day, not necessarily because he had reached his destination?
answers: He left Beersheba
He went toward Haran
He stayed there because the sun had set
challenge.explanation: The stated reason for stopping was that the sun had set, suggesting that he stopped for the night along the way.

questions.question: What does the phrase “he lighted upon a certain place” mean in context?
answers: Jacob came upon a place during his journey
Jacob struck a person
Jacob built the place
questions.explanation: Here the phrase means that Jacob arrived at or came upon a place during his journey.

questions.question: What can we infer from Jacob putting stones under his head?
answers: He slept in a well-furnished house
He was sleeping outdoors and used stones as a support for his head
He gathered stones to build a city
questions.explanation: The passage describes no bed or house, so Jacob apparently used stones as a support beneath his head.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Jacob stopped because of the time of day, not necessarily because he had reached his destination?
answers: He left Beersheba
He went toward Haran
He stayed there because the sun had set
questions.explanation: The stated reason for stopping was that the sun had set, suggesting that he stopped for the night along the way.

paragraphs.title: Jacob’s Dream and the Promise of the Land

easy.question: What did Jacob see in his dream?
answers: A ladder reaching to heaven
A great city
A wide river
easy.explanation: Jacob saw a ladder set up on the earth whose top reached to heaven.

easy.question: Who went up and down the ladder?
answers: Human beings
The angels of God
Shepherds
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the angels of God ascending and descending on it.”

easy.question: What did the Lord promise Jacob concerning the land?
answers: That he would live in a palace
That he and his descendants would receive the land
That he would sell the land
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “The land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed.”

medium.question: In the phrase “thou shalt spread abroad,” what does “spread abroad” mean?
answers: Grow and extend widely
Stop in one place
Disappear quickly
medium.explanation: In the context of the four directions, “spread abroad” means that Jacob’s descendants would multiply and extend widely.

medium.question: What connection exists between the promise of the land and the promise of descendants?
answers: The land would be given only to one person
The land and the descendants are both part of Jacob’s continuing blessing
The descendants would have to leave the land
medium.explanation: The Lord promises both the land to Jacob and his descendants and a great multitude of descendants.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the promises given to Jacob?
answers: Protection on the journey, the promise of land, and the appearance of the angels
The promise of land and descendants, followed by protection and a return to the land
A return to the land, the appearance of the angels, and the promise of descendants
medium.explanation: First the Lord promises the land and descendants; then he promises to be with Jacob, protect him, and bring him back to the land.

challenge.question: Why can the ladder be understood as symbolizing a connection between earth and heaven?
answers: It was set up on earth and its top reached heaven
It was made of ancient stone
It was inside a house
challenge.explanation: The ladder extended from earth to heaven, and the angels moved up and down it, linking the two realms.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the phrase “to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”?
answers: The descendants would remain in a small area
The descendants would spread in every direction
The descendants would move only southward
challenge.explanation: The four directions emphasize the wide expansion of Jacob’s descendants.

challenge.question: What is distinctive about the Lord’s promise in verse 15?
answers: The Lord promises to accompany and protect Jacob wherever he goes
The Lord promises that Jacob will never leave the land
The Lord promises that Jacob will never grow old
challenge.explanation: The Lord says, “I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest,” including places outside the land.

questions.question: Why can the ladder be understood as symbolizing a connection between earth and heaven?
answers: It was set up on earth and its top reached heaven
It was made of ancient stone
It was inside a house
questions.explanation: The ladder extended from earth to heaven, and the angels moved up and down it, linking the two realms.

questions.question: What can we infer from the phrase “to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”?
answers: The descendants would remain in a small area
The descendants would spread in every direction
The descendants would move only southward
questions.explanation: The four directions emphasize the wide expansion of Jacob’s descendants.

questions.question: What is distinctive about the Lord’s promise in verse 15?
answers: The Lord promises to accompany and protect Jacob wherever he goes
The Lord promises that Jacob will never leave the land
The Lord promises that Jacob will never grow old
questions.explanation: The Lord says, “I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest,” including places outside the land.

easy.question: What did Jacob realize after he awoke?
answers: The Lord was in that place
He had arrived home
He needed to return to Haran
easy.explanation: Jacob said, “Surely the Lord is in this place,” realizing that the Lord was there.

easy.question: How did Jacob feel after this realization?
answers: Very happy
Afraid and overwhelmed
Angry
easy.explanation: The verse says that Jacob was afraid.

easy.question: What did Jacob call the place?
answers: A great field
The king’s city
The house of God and the gate of heaven
easy.explanation: Jacob said, “this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.”

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: Jacob awoke, realized the Lord was there, and then became afraid
Jacob became afraid, fell asleep, and then awoke
Jacob called the place the house of God, and then fell asleep
medium.explanation: Jacob first awoke, then realized that the Lord was in the place, and afterward the verse says that he was afraid.

medium.question: Why did Jacob say, “and I knew it not”?
answers: He had forgotten his name
Before this, he did not know that the Lord was in that place
He did not know where to go
medium.explanation: Jacob admitted that before the dream he did not know that the place was special or that the Lord was present there.

medium.question: In the phrase “How dreadful is this place,” what does “dreadful” mean?
answers: Small and ordinary
Far away and isolated
A place that inspires awe and holiness
medium.explanation: In this context, “dreadful” describes a place that inspires fear, reverence, and a sense of holiness.

challenge.question: What does Jacob’s phrase “this is none other but” express?
answers: The clear recognition that the place is the house of God and the gate of heaven
Doubt that anything special was there
A desire to leave immediately
challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses clear recognition that the place is not ordinary but the house of God and the gate of heaven.

challenge.question: What change took place in Jacob’s understanding from the beginning to the end of his words?
answers: He went from fear to sleep
He went from not knowing to recognizing the holiness of the place
He went from joy to anger
challenge.explanation: At first Jacob said he did not know the Lord was there; afterward he understood the place’s spiritual significance and called it the house of God.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Jacob calling the place both “the house of God” and “the gate of heaven”?
answers: The place was an ordinary dwelling
The place was higher than all the mountains
The place was understood as a point of connection between earth and heaven
challenge.explanation: These names express Jacob’s understanding that the place connected God’s presence on earth with heaven.

questions.question: What does Jacob’s phrase “this is none other but” express?
answers: The clear recognition that the place is the house of God and the gate of heaven
Doubt that anything special was there
A desire to leave immediately
questions.explanation: The phrase expresses clear recognition that the place is not ordinary but the house of God and the gate of heaven.

questions.question: What change took place in Jacob’s understanding from the beginning to the end of his words?
answers: He went from fear to sleep
He went from not knowing to recognizing the holiness of the place
He went from joy to anger
questions.explanation: At first Jacob said he did not know the Lord was there; afterward he understood the place’s spiritual significance and called it the house of God.

questions.question: What can we infer from Jacob calling the place both “the house of God” and “the gate of heaven”?
answers: The place was an ordinary dwelling
The place was higher than all the mountains
The place was understood as a point of connection between earth and heaven
questions.explanation: These names express Jacob’s understanding that the place connected God’s presence on earth with heaven.

paragraphs.title: The Pillar and the Naming of Bethel

easy.question: What did Jacob do with the stone he had placed near his head?
answers: He set it up as a pillar
He threw it away
He hid it
easy.explanation: Jacob took the stone and set it up as a pillar.

easy.question: What did Jacob pour on top of the stone?
answers: Water
Oil
Wine
easy.explanation: The verse says that Jacob poured oil upon the top of the stone.

easy.question: What name did Jacob give the place?
answers: Luz
Jerusalem
Bethel
easy.explanation: Jacob called the place Bethel.

medium.question: What did Jacob do immediately after taking the stone?
answers: He set it up as a pillar
He called the place Luz
He left the place
medium.explanation: After taking the stone, Jacob set it up as a pillar.

medium.question: In the phrase “the stone that he had put for his pillows,” what does “pillows” mean?
answers: A place for his feet
Supports for his head
The center of the city
medium.explanation: The stone had been placed near Jacob’s head while he slept.

medium.question: What is the relationship between the names Bethel and Luz?
answers: Bethel was Jacob’s name and Luz was the stone’s name
Luz was the new name of the place and Bethel was its old name
Jacob called the place Bethel, while Luz was its former name
medium.explanation: The verse says Jacob called the place Bethel, although the city had formerly been called Luz.

challenge.question: What can we understand from Jacob pouring oil on top of the pillar?
answers: He dedicated or set apart the place
He used the stone as a cooking vessel
He wanted to put the stone back
challenge.explanation: Pouring oil on the pillar expresses an act of dedication and setting the place apart.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the stone made into a pillar was the same stone Jacob had used earlier?
answers: The city was called Luz
Jacob took the stone that he had put for his pillows
The act took place in the morning
challenge.explanation: The phrase “the stone that he had put for his pillows” connects the stone used at night with the pillar.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the distinction between “that place” and “that city”?
answers: Jacob changed the name of the whole land
There was no city there
Jacob gave the place a new name, while the city already had an earlier name
challenge.explanation: The verse distinguishes between the place Jacob called Bethel and the city formerly called Luz.

questions.question: What can we understand from Jacob pouring oil on top of the pillar?
answers: He dedicated or set apart the place
He used the stone as a cooking vessel
He wanted to put the stone back
questions.explanation: Pouring oil on the pillar expresses an act of dedication and setting the place apart.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the stone made into a pillar was the same stone Jacob had used earlier?
answers: The city was called Luz
Jacob took the stone that he had put for his pillows
The act took place in the morning
questions.explanation: The phrase “the stone that he had put for his pillows” connects the stone used at night with the pillar.

questions.question: What can we infer from the distinction between “that place” and “that city”?
answers: Jacob changed the name of the whole land
There was no city there
Jacob gave the place a new name, while the city already had an earlier name
questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes between the place Jacob called Bethel and the city formerly called Luz.

easy.question: What did Jacob vow that the Lord would do for him on the journey?
answers: Protect him
Give him an army
Build him a house
easy.explanation: Jacob asked that the Lord be with him and keep him on the way he traveled.

easy.question: To whose house did Jacob ask to return in peace?
answers: To the land of Egypt
To his father’s house
To Laban’s house
easy.explanation: Jacob said, “So that I come again to my father’s house in peace.”

easy.question: What would Jacob’s pillar become?
answers: A tool
A grave marker
The house of God
easy.explanation: Jacob said that the stone he had set up as a pillar would be God’s house.

medium.question: What is the central condition in Jacob’s vow?
answers: That the Lord would be with him and protect him
That he would find work
That he would remain on the road forever
medium.explanation: Jacob describes his requests to God and connects his vow to the Lord’s presence and protection.

medium.question: In the phrase “come again to my father’s house in peace,” what does “in peace” mean?
answers: Secretly
Safely and unharmed
Quickly
medium.explanation: Because Jacob asks for the Lord’s protection, “in peace” means returning safely and unharmed.

medium.question: Which sequence correctly describes Jacob’s words?
answers: Returning to his father’s house, eating, and setting out
Setting up the stone, building a house, and receiving clothes
Protection on the journey, food and clothing, and returning to his father’s house
medium.explanation: Jacob asks for protection, bread, and clothing, and then speaks of returning to his father’s house.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “then shall the Lord be my God” show about the meaning of Jacob’s return?
answers: His return would be connected with a renewed relationship with the Lord
Jacob would stop believing in the Lord
He would return only to collect possessions
challenge.explanation: Jacob connects his safe return with the Lord being his God, so the return is spiritual as well as geographical.

challenge.question: Why does Jacob mention both bread and clothing in his vow?
answers: To describe a special feast
To ask for his basic needs during the journey
To promise gifts for his family
challenge.explanation: Bread and clothing represent the basic necessities Jacob asks to receive during his journey.

challenge.question: What does Jacob’s commitment to give a tenth of everything he receives mean?
answers: He promises to give away all his possessions
He promises to give nothing
He expresses gratitude and dedication to the Lord
challenge.explanation: A tenth is a portion of one’s possessions dedicated to the Lord, expressing gratitude and recognition that blessings come from him.

questions.question: What does the phrase “then shall the Lord be my God” show about the meaning of Jacob’s return?
answers: His return would be connected with a renewed relationship with the Lord
Jacob would stop believing in the Lord
He would return only to collect possessions
questions.explanation: Jacob connects his safe return with the Lord being his God, so the return is spiritual as well as geographical.
